mainTopic: How many of each of the ארבעה מינים to take, the ruling on cut-tipped הדסים, and which kinds of אתרוג are פסול or כשר
overview: The amud opens with the last line of an earlier discussion: knowing that a place's name changed matters for writing a גט correctly. Then a new משנה asks how many of each of the ארבעה מינים to take. רבי ישמעאל says three הדסים, two ערבות, one לולב and one אתרוג, and allows two of the הדסים to be קטומים. רבי טרפון allows all three to be קטומים, and רבי עקיבא says one of each species is enough. A ברייתא gives רבי ישמעאל's source in the פסוק, and רבי אליעזר shows that the אתרוג stands apart from the bundle. The ברייתא then learns from ״ולקחתם״ that all four species are required together. The גמרא challenges רבי ישמעאל's middle position and answers that he retracted it. שמואל rules like רבי טרפון, and he threatened overcharging myrtle sellers with that view rather than רבי עקיבא's, because in practice cut-tipped הדסים are easy to find. A new משנה then lists which kinds of אתרוג are פסול or כשר, based on their origin, physical damage, color and size.

steps.title: Why the name change matters: bills of divorce
steps.stepSummary: The previous discussion about place names that changed ends by saying that the practical difference is for writing a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference? It matters for women's bills of divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the topic on the previous amud. It asks why it matters that a place's name changed, and it answers that it matters for גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a גט is written, the name of the place must be written exactly right. So a scribe has to know what a place is called now. This line closes that side discussion before the new משנה begins.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference comes out of this?

steps.whatToRemember: Once this line ends, the topic changes completely to the ארבעה מינים.

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?
For women's bills of divorce.
phrases.notes: A גט must record place names accurately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion earlier about renamed places.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Knowing that a place's name changed matters for writing גיטין correctly.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: three myrtles, two willows, one לולב, one אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens with רבי ישמעאל's count of each species. He also allows two of the three הדסים to have cut tips.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי ישמעאל says: three myrtle branches and two willow branches, one לולב and one אתרוג. This is valid even if two of the myrtles have their tips cut off and only one does not.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי ישמעאל tells us how many of each species to take, and he is lenient about cut-tipped הדסים as long as at least one is whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The numbers differ from species to species: three, two, one and one. On the קטום question, his rule is that two cut-tipped branches are fine, but at least one of the three must still be whole.

keyTerms.meaning: With the top tip cut off

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Rabbi Yishmael says:
three myrtle branches and two willow branches,
one lulav and one etrog.
Even if two have their tips cut off,
and one does not have its tip cut off, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new chapter topic, unrelated to the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Take 3 הדסים, 2 ערבות, 1 לולב and 1 אתרוג. Two cut-tipped הדסים are acceptable if one is whole.

steps.title: רבי טרפון: even all three myrtles may be cut
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון is even more lenient. All three הדסים may be קטומים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון says: Even if all three have their tips cut off, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the משנה, about the cut-tipped הדסים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון agrees that three הדסים are needed, but he does not require any of them to be whole. For him, a cut tip never disqualifies a הדס.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי טרפון is not arguing about the number three. He argues only about whether the tips may be cut.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon says:
Even if all three have their tips cut off, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי ישמעאל on the cut-tipped הדסים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three הדסים that are all cut-tipped are valid.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: just one of each species
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא compares the הדס and ערבה to the לולב and אתרוג. Just as those are one each, so are these.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: Just as there is one לולב and one אתרוג, so too there is one myrtle and one willow.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the משנה. It disagrees with the numbers that רבי ישמעאל gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא uses a comparison. Since the לולב and אתרוג are clearly one each, he treats all four species the same way. So one הדס and one ערבה are enough.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
Just as there is one lulav and one etrog,
so too there is one myrtle and one willow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי ישמעאל about how many of each species are needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One of each species is enough.

steps.title: The verse-based source for רבי ישמעאל's numbers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows how רבי ישמעאל reads each phrase in the פסוק to arrive at 1, 1, 3 and 2.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught in a ברייתא that רבי ישמעאל says: "The fruit of a beautiful tree" means one. "Branches of date palms" means one. "Boughs of a thick tree" means three. "Willows of the brook" means two. It is valid even if two are cut-tipped and one is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the source in the פסוק for the numbers in רבי ישמעאל's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase gives a number. פרי is singular, so one. כפת is written without a ו, so it is read as one. ענף עץ עבות describes a branch covered with layers of leaves, which points to three. ערבי נחל is plural, and the smallest plural is two.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Fruit of a beautiful tree, which is the אתרוג
Branches of date palms, which is the לולב
Boughs of a thick tree, which is the הדס

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי ישמעאל's numbers come from careful reading of the פסוק and are not arbitrary.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yishmael says:
"The fruit of a beautiful tree" means one.
"Branches of date palms" means one.
phrases.notes: כפת is written without a ו, so it is read as singular.

phrases.english: "Boughs of a thick tree" means three.
"Willows of the brook" means two.
phrases.notes: Plural, and the minimum plural is two.

phrases.english: And even if two have their tips cut off,
and one does not have its tip cut off, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the verse-based source for רבי ישמעאל's opinion in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ישמעאל's numbers: 1 אתרוג, 1 לולב, 3 הדסים, 2 ערבות

steps.title: רבי טרפון in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא repeats רבי טרפון's view and states clearly that he also requires three הדסים, even if all are cut-tipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון says: Three, and even if all three are cut-tipped.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא presents רבי טרפון's opinion, adding the word "three" that the משנה left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added word שלשה confirms what we assumed in the משנה. רבי טרפון agrees with רבי ישמעאל about the number three and disagrees only about the cut tips.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon says:
Three, and even if all three have their tips cut off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the second opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three הדסים are required, and all three may be cut-tipped.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא repeats רבי עקיבא's comparison: one of each species.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: Just as there is one לולב and one אתרוג, so too there is one myrtle and one willow.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא presents רבי עקיבא's view. This sets up רבי אליעזר's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is the same as in the משנה. It is repeated here because רבי אליעזר is about to respond to this comparison.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
Just as there is one lulav and one etrog,
so too there is one myrtle and one willow.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁלּוּלָב אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the third opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One of each species is enough.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the etrog stands apart from the other species
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר points out that the פסוק separates the אתרוג from the other three species. The אתרוג is not bundled with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: One might think the אתרוג should be bound with the others in one bundle. But you can respond: Does the verse say "the fruit of a beautiful tree AND branches of date palms"? It only says "branches," with no "and."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר responds to רבי עקיבא. He shows from the פסוק that the אתרוג is in a separate category from the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the לולב, הדס and ערבה are joined by "and," but there is no "and" before כפת. This means the אתרוג is held separately and not tied into the bundle. Since the אתרוג is treated differently, it is a weak model for setting the number of the other species, and this weakens רבי עקיבא's "just as" comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it not so that

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse רבי אליעזר's point with the question of how many to take. His proof is about the bundle: the missing "ו" shows that the אתרוג stays outside the אגודה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
One might think the etrog should be with them
in one bundle.
You can say: Does it say
"The fruit of a beautiful tree and branches of date palms"?
Does it not say only "branches," without "and"?
phrases.notes: The missing ו separates the אתרוג from the bundle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי עקיבא's comparison of the הדס and ערבה to the אתרוג.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's comparison between the אתרוג and the other species
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק sets the אתרוג apart from the others because there is no "and" before it, so it cannot serve as a model for the other species.

steps.title: Source that all four species are required together
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know that missing one species prevents the מצוה from being fulfilled with the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that they prevent one another?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new question and sets up the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the אתרוג is held separately, we still need a source that all the species must be taken together. If one is missing, the מצוה is not fulfilled with the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know
They hold each other back: each one is required

phrases.english: And from where do we know that they prevent one another?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After separating the אתרוג from the bundle, asks for the source that all four species are still required together.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source in the פסוק that every species is required for the מצוה.

steps.title: "And you shall take" means a complete taking
steps.stepSummary: The word ״ולקחתם״ teaches that the taking must be complete, with all four species.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says "And you shall take," which teaches that it must be a complete taking.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question with a derivation from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ולקחתם is read as לקיחה תמה, a complete taking. So the מצוה is one combined act, and taking only some of the species does not count.
steps.whatToRemember: Separate from the debate about numbers, all four species are מעכבין: if one is missing, the מצוה is not fulfilled.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical הלכה that a person who lacks one of the four species cannot fulfill the מצוה with the others.

phrases.english: The verse states: "And you shall take"
so that it shall be a complete taking.
phrases.notes: The derivation plays on the similar sound of ולקחתם and לקיחה תמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ולקחתם means a complete taking, so all four species are required.

steps.title: Challenging רבי ישמעאל's middle position
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רבי ישמעאל's view that two הדסים may be cut-tipped while one must be whole. Either way you look at it, the view seems inconsistent.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל, whichever way you look at it, has a problem. If he requires whole branches, he should require all of them to be whole. If he does not require whole branches, then not even one should need to be whole!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ישמעאל. His view seems to sit awkwardly between two logical options.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל required three הדסים, two of which may be cut-tipped while one must be whole. The גמרא argues that wholeness is either required or it is not. If it is required, all three should be whole. If it is not required, why must even one be whole?

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it (a two-sided challenge)
Whole (here: myrtle branches whose tips are not cut off)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael, whichever way you look at it?
phrases.notes: A 'מה נפשך' sets up a challenge from both sides.

phrases.english: If he requires whole ones,
let him also require all of them to be whole;
if he does not require whole ones,
phrases.notes: Option two: wholeness does not matter.

phrases.english: then not even one should need to be whole!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the source for needing all four species back to analyzing the three views on the הדסים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's view: three הדסים, two may be cut-tipped, one must be whole
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided dilemma: wholeness is either required, so all must be whole, or not required, so none must be whole. A middle position looks inconsistent.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל retracted
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי, quoted by בִּירָאָה, says רבי ישמעאל took back his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: בִּירָאָה said in the name of רבי אמי: רבי ישמעאל retracted his view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying רבי ישמעאל changed his mind and no longer holds that view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not defend the middle position. It admits the challenge is strong and says רבי ישמעאל himself retracted. According to Sefaria's explanation, he came to agree that only one הדס is needed, and it must be whole.

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted / took back his view

phrases.english: Bira'a said that Rabbi Ami said:
Rabbi Yishmael retracted his view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: the view being challenged was abandoned by its author
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל holds an inconsistent middle position.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל no longer holds that position.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי טרפון, who allows three הדסים even if all are cut-tipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that שמואל said: the הלכה is like רבי טרפון.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives the practical ruling on the הדסים: we follow רבי טרפון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Out of the three views (רבי ישמעאל, רבי טרפון, רבי עקיבא), שמואל chooses רבי טרפון. That means three הדסים are needed, but all of them may have cut tips.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who requires three הדסים, even if all are cut-tipped

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה (per שמואל) follows רבי טרפון: three הדסים, even all cut-tipped.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Tarfon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting aside רבי ישמעאל's view, the גמרא gives the practical ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי טרפון regarding cut-tipped הדסים.

steps.title: שמואל's warning to the myrtle sellers
steps.stepSummary: A story shows שמואל holds this view consistently. He warned myrtle sellers to charge fair prices or he would publicly teach like רבי טרפון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל follows his own reasoning here. שמואל said to the myrtle sellers: 'Charge a fair price and sell. If not, I will publicly teach the law for you like רבי טרפון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to show that שמואל really does hold like רבי טרפון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people knew cut-tipped הדסים were כשר, demand for expensive whole הדסים would drop, and so would their price. שמואל used this as leverage against overcharging, which shows he truly considered רבי טרפון's view to be the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own line of reasoning (is consistent)
Make it equal, meaning charge a fair price

phrases.english: And Shmuel follows his own reasoning,
for Shmuel said
to those who were selling myrtle:
Make the price fair and sell;
and if not, I will publicly teach for you
in accordance with Rabbi Tarfon.
phrases.notes: That is, he would announce that cut-tipped myrtles are fine, which would lower demand for whole ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 13 by showing שמואל acted consistently with his ruling.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי טרפון
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's threat to the myrtle sellers

steps.title: Why not threaten with רבי עקיבא's easier view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל chose רבי טרפון. If the point was leniency, רבי עקיבא, who needs only one הדס, seems even more lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? If you say it is because רבי טרפון is lenient, then let שמואל teach them like רבי עקיבא, who is even more lenient!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the story: if שמואל wanted to scare the sellers with a lenient ruling, why not pick the most lenient one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא requires only one הדס, which seems easier than three. So a threat based on רבי עקיבא's view would lower demand even more. The question is why שמואל chose רבי טרפון.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
If you say it is because he is lenient,
then let him teach them according to Rabbi Akiva,
who is even more lenient!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the logic of the story in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's choice of רבי טרפון as the threat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If leniency was the goal, רבי עקיבא's one-branch view seems more lenient and would have been the better threat.

steps.title: In practice, רבי טרפון's view is easier
steps.stepSummary: Three cut-tipped הדסים are easy to find, but one whole הדס is rare. So in practice רבי טרפון's view is the more lenient one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three cut-tipped branches are common, but one branch that is not cut-tipped is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי טרפון is actually the easier view in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא needs only one branch, but that branch must be whole, and whole branches are hard to find. Having to buy one whole branch keeps the sellers' expensive product in demand. Only רבי טרפון's view frees buyers from needing any whole branch at all.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't count only the number of branches. רבי עקיבא needs fewer branches, but they must be whole, which is the hard part. So רבי טרפון is the practical leniency.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי טרפון's view is the most lenient in practice, because whole הדסים are rare and cut-tipped ones are common.

phrases.english: Three cut-tipped branches are common;
one that is not cut-tipped is not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality: what is easy to find decides which view is truly lenient
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא is more lenient because he requires fewer branches.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי טרפון is more lenient in practice because cut-tipped branches are easy to find and whole ones are rare.

steps.title: משנה: kinds of etrog that are unfit
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists kinds of אתרוג that are פסול: stolen, dry, from an אשרה or an עיר הנדחת, ערלה, and impure תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An אתרוג that is stolen or dry is פסול. One from an אשרה or from an עיר הנדחת is פסול. One of ערלה is פסול. One of impure תרומה is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists kinds of אתרוג that cannot be used for the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are all disqualified outright. A stolen אתרוג is not truly yours, and a dry one lacks beauty. One from an אשרה or an עיר הנדחת is forbidden because of idolatry. ערלה and impure תרומה are forbidden for benefit, or must be burned, so they do not count as usable property.

keyTerms.meaning: A city led astray to idolatry, whose property is destroyed
Fruit from a tree's first three years, forbidden for benefit
Impure תרומה, which must be burned

phrases.english: MISHNA: A stolen or dry etrog is unfit.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל אֲשֵׁרָה וְשֶׁל עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: One from an asheira or from an idolatrous city is unfit.
One of orla is unfit.
One of impure teruma is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה; the discussion of הדסים has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stolen, dry, idolatrous, ערלה, or impure תרומה אתרוג is פסול.

steps.title: Pure תרומה: not ideal, but valid after the fact
steps.stepSummary: An אתרוג of pure תרומה should not be taken from the start, but if someone did take it, it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of pure תרומה, he should not take it; but if he took it, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now moves to a softer category: an אתרוג that should not be used from the start but works after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pure תרומה can still be eaten by a כהן, so it is not forbidden property like the earlier cases. Ideally one should not handle it for the מצוה, possibly because handling might make it impure. Still, after the fact the מצוה is fulfilled.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure תרומה, edible by a כהן
He should not take it (from the start)
But if he took it, it is valid (after the fact)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse this with impure תרומה in the previous step. Impure is פסול; pure is only discouraged and is כשר after the fact.

phrases.english: One of pure teruma, one should not take it;
but if he took it, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with impure תרומה in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אתרוג of pure תרומה should not be used from the start, but it is כשר after the fact.

steps.title: דמאי: a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: For an אתרוג of דמאי, בית שמאי say it is פסול and בית הלל say it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of דמאי: בית שמאי disqualify it, and בית הלל declare it כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה records a disagreement about an אתרוג of דמאי, produce whose tithes are uncertain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דמאי is bought from an עם הארץ who may not have tithed. בית שמאי treat it as unusable for the מצוה. בית הלל allow it. The משנה itself gives no reason; the גמרא discusses the reasoning later.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce of doubtful tithing, bought from an עם הארץ

phrases.english: One of demai:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי פּוֹסְלִין, וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַכְשִׁירִין.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai deem it unfit, and Beit Hillel deem it fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list with a disputed case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דמאי: בית שמאי say פסול, בית הלל say כשר.

steps.title: Second tithe in Jerusalem: valid after the fact
steps.stepSummary: An אתרוג of מעשר שני in ירושלים should not be taken from the start, but if someone took it, it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of מעשר שני in ירושלים, he should not take it; but if he took it, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends this list with מעשר שני, which follows the same pattern as pure תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני may be eaten in ירושלים, so it is usable. Even so, there are concerns about it, so ideally it should not be used for the מצוה. After the fact it works.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three levels: some cases are פסול outright; pure תרומה and מעשר שני are 'should not take, but כשר after the fact'; and דמאי is disputed.

phrases.english: One of second tithe in Jerusalem:
one should not take it; and if he took it, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels the pure תרומה rule in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אתרוג of מעשר שני in ירושלים should not be used from the start, but it is כשר after the fact.

steps.title: Physical damage that makes an אתרוג invalid
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists types of damage that make an אתרוג פסול: blemishes on most of it, a removed tip, peeling, splitting, or a hole where something is missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If blister-like spots grew over most of the אתרוג, or its tip at the top was removed, or it was peeled, or split, or pierced with even a tiny bit missing, it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from problems with where an אתרוג comes from to problems with its physical condition. It lists kinds of damage that make it פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier cases like stolen or ערלה were about the אתרוג's status. Here the issue is its body: the אתרוג must look whole and beautiful. Blemishes on the majority, or any missing piece, ruin that.

keyTerms.meaning: Blister-like or scab-like spots on the skin of the fruit
Its tip, the small knob at the top (blossom end) of the אתרוג
Is missing even a tiny amount

phrases.english: If blister-like spots grew over most of it,
phrases.notes: רוב = majority of the fruit's surface.

phrases.english: if its tip was removed,
phrases.notes: The פטמה is the knob at the top, opposite the stem.

phrases.english: if it was peeled, if it was split,
if it was pierced and is missing any amount —
phrases.notes: The key word is 'missing'. Compare the next step.

phrases.english: it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of פסול kinds of אתרוג that began in step 17. It moves from problems of origin and status to physical damage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אתרוג is פסול if it has חזזית on its majority, a removed פטמה, is peeled or split, or has a hole with something missing.

steps.title: Similar damage that still leaves the אתרוג valid
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the matching list of lighter damage that does not make an אתרוג פסול: blemishes on only a small part, a removed stem, or a hole with nothing missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If blister-like spots grew on only a small part of it, or its stem was removed, or it was pierced but nothing is missing, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the opposite list. These are cases that look like the ones before, but the אתרוג stays כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case answers one from the previous step. Blemishes on the majority are פסול, but on a minority they are כשר. Losing the top tip is פסול, but losing the stem at the bottom is fine. A hole with a missing piece is פסול, but a hole with nothing missing is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: A small part of it (the minority)
Its stem, the part that attached it to the tree

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the פטמה and the עוקץ. The פטמה is the knob at the top, and removing it makes the אתרוג פסול. The עוקץ is the stem at the bottom, and removing it leaves the אתרוג כשר. Also notice that 'pierced' appears in both lists. What decides the case is whether something is actually missing.
steps.whatToRemember: Majority versus minority, top tip versus bottom stem, and missing versus not missing. These three contrasts sort the physical damage into פסול and כשר.

phrases.english: If blister-like spots grew on a small part of it,
if its stem was removed,
phrases.notes: The stem at the bottom, where it hung from the tree.

phrases.english: if it was pierced but is not missing any amount —
it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the mirror image of step 21. Each lenient case matches one of the strict cases there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אתרוג is כשר if it has חזזית on only a minority, a removed עוקץ, or a hole with nothing missing.

steps.title: Color: a black אתרוג and a leek-green אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: A very dark (כושי) אתרוג is פסול. For a leek-green אתרוג, רבי מאיר says it is כשר and רבי יהודה says it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: A black (כושי) אתרוג is פסול. As for one that is green like a leek, רבי מאיר says it is כשר and רבי יהודה says it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns from damage to color. It gives one clear ruling and then one dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees a black אתרוג is פסול because it does not look like a normal אתרוג. A deep green one is less clear. רבי מאיר accepts it, while רבי יהודה rejects it, probably because it is not ripe or does not look like a proper אתרוג.

keyTerms.meaning: Black or very dark, like a person from Cush

phrases.english: A black (Cushite) etrog — is invalid,
and one green like a leek —
Rabbi Meir rules it valid
and Rabbi Yehuda rules it invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from physical damage to the color of the אתרוג.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כושי אתרוג is פסול. For a leek-green אתרוג, רבי מאיר rules it כשר and רבי יהודה rules it פסול.

steps.title: The smallest size allowed for an אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says the smallest allowed אתרוג is the size of a walnut. רבי יהודה says it is the size of an egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the minimum size of a small אתרוג? רבי מאיר says the size of a walnut. רבי יהודה says the size of an egg.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now turns to size and starts with the smallest אתרוג that is still כשר. Two תנאים give different measures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Below a certain size the fruit is not considered a real, proper אתרוג. רבי מאיר is more lenient and allows a smaller fruit (a walnut). רבי יהודה requires a larger one (an egg).

phrases.english: The measure of a small etrog —
Rabbi Meir says: like a walnut,
Rabbi Yehuda says: like an egg.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic in the משנה, the size limits of an אתרוג.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The minimum size of an אתרוג is a walnut according to רבי מאיר and an egg according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The largest size allowed for an אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says an אתרוג may be no bigger than a size where one could hold two in one hand. רבי יוסי says even an אתרוג so big that it takes two hands to hold one is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a large אתרוג, the limit is a size where a person could hold two of them in one hand. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says it is כשר even if it takes both hands to hold just one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the size topic with the largest allowed אתרוג. רבי יהודה sets a maximum, and רבי יוסי disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה sets an upper limit: the אתרוג must be small enough that two would fit in one hand. רבי יוסי holds there is effectively no upper limit. Even a huge אתרוג that needs two hands is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The words of (marks whose opinion this is)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה's measure of 'two in one hand' does not mean you hold two אתרוגים. It is only a way to describe the maximum size of one אתרוג.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives size limits on both ends. For the minimum: walnut (רבי מאיר) or egg (רבי יהודה). For the maximum: רבי יהודה sets a limit of two in one hand, and רבי יוסי allows even one that needs two hands.

phrases.english: And for a large one — enough that one could hold two in his one hand.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
And Rabbi Yosei says:
Even one in his two hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the size topic. After the minimum size in step 24, it now gives the maximum size.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה sets the maximum size of an אתרוג at two fitting in one hand. רבי יוסי holds that even one needing two hands is כשר.
